reviews.text: Thank you so much for the great rating! We’re happy to know you had a positive experience. Your support truly means a lot!

I recently visited Vetco at Petco for flea and tick medication for my American Bully, and unfortunately, my experience with Dr. Amber Nava was very disappointing.

When I arrived, I asked the front-desk staff whether my dog needed to remain in the clinic after being weighed. I was told that he did not, so I returned him to my air-conditioned car. I was later informed that he needed to come back inside because the medication required a veterinary examination. I immediately brought him back and explained that he is an American Bully who can become anxious and nervous in unfamiliar environments.

I was very clear about his anxiety and wanted to make sure the examination could be performed safely and comfortably. Unfortunately, Dr. Nava did not appear comfortable or confident handling my anxious dog. She asked whether my dog had ever bitten anyone, which I understand is a reasonable safety question. However, when I asked what the examination would involve so that I could properly assist her, I did not receive a clear explanation.

I specifically asked whether she needed to examine his teeth or mouth, but my question was not answered. Because I wanted to protect both my dog and Dr. Nava, I requested that he be muzzled before the examination. The muzzle that was placed on him appeared to be excessively tight, and he began panting heavily. Dr. Nava subsequently assessed his breathing, even though he was visibly stressed and panting while wearing the muzzle.

My issue was not that an examination was required. I was completely willing to cooperate and assist in whatever examination was necessary. My concern was the lack of communication, patience, and apparent comfort in handling an anxious dog. An American Bully is a strong, powerful breed, and I believe veterinary professionals working with larger dogs should have the training and confidence necessary to safely and calmly handle them, particularly when the owner has already explained that the dog is anxious.

I do want to recognize Marissa and Kaitlyn, who were both excellent. They were friendly, helpful, and professional throughout the visit, and I genuinely appreciate their assistance. Ultimately, I was able to obtain the flea and tick medication my dog needed.

However, the interaction with Dr. Amber Nava left me concerned about how anxious dogs are handled at this location. I hope Vetco management takes this feedback seriously and considers additional training and protocols for working with anxious and larger-breed dogs. Better communication and a calmer, more confident approach would have made this a significantly better experience for everyone involved.

I’ve seen three different vets in the River Oaks area over the past year, and each visit felt more disappointing—and more expensive—than the last. A friend recommended I try Vetco at the Petco on Shepherd, and I’ll admit I was skeptical. No flashy lobby, no big marketing push, none of the “boutique vet” amenities you see around here. But after my first visit, I realized quickly that none of the optics matter when the care is genuinely good.

Every visit since, (I think I am up to 5 or 6 now), has reinforced that this is the most honest, straightforward veterinary team I’ve found in Houston (perhaps anywhere in the big cities I've lived with pets in the US).

To illustrate - Today, during a routine wellness check, I asked about getting my dog’s nails trimmed. Instead of adding another charge, they told me I’d save money by having the groomer do it. That kind of honesty is rare. Keep in mind, it was only $10 extra and at that point my pup was accustomed to Christian and Valentin. But it was the principle that mattered to me.

The real reeason I moved my business to Vetco is one of the previous vets (not to be named, but also in River Oaks) insisted I was neglecting my dog by not commissioning a heart worm test 6 months after completing our heartworm injection/treatment protocol. This is the same Vet that advised me to get a leptospirosis update shot a week before the heartworm treatment was scheduled - which my pup got very ill afterwards and complicated the heartworm treatment. That was a $350 mistake I didn't make but certainly paid for.

Thats when I started going to the Vetco for another opinion about working through the longer term care needed for heartwork treatment recovery. The Vetco doctor at the time (I believe his name was Craig), not only disagreed with the other last vet, he even printed out a research paper explaining why make sense until at least 9 months—and to make me feel comfortable my pup was at no further risk, he then checked my dog’s vitals thoroughly to help me avoid the costs an unnecessary test would have been that the previous vet had recommended after giving me bad advise.

Today I met Dr. Valentin Medina and a Vet Assistant Christian, and the experience was superb. Most vets take your pet to the back holding area, out of sight. Dr. Medina brought everything into the room so my dog stayed comfortable and calm together with me. It’s a small gesture, but it says a lot about how they operate.

If you’ve been struggling to find a vet who doesn't treat you like an invoice, and who actually helps you understand how to keep your pet healthy—Vetco on Shepherd is worth the switch. Dr. Valentin and his team clearly prioritize your pet’s well‑being over up selling services. They’ve earned my trust, and they’ve changed the way I see veterinary care. They also follow-up so quickly, it's astounding. I had my records from the visit in hand within 30 minutes of the appointment!

Bravo to the Vetco Houston South Shepherd team. I hope I won’t need to visit often, but when I do, I know I’ll get honest advice, fair pricing, and real care for my dog. Truly a top‑tier establishment.

I was a little worried given some of these reviews and I don’t want to invalidate anyone’s experience, but today I took my sweet old cat here for flea treatment / prevention and everyone was awesome. While I only booked for flea treatment, Dr. McGovern gave my cat a full exam and even addressed other concerns I had about my cat. Dr. McGovern and Blair (sorry if I am misspelling anyone’s name) were both kind and gentle with my cat. Thank you for your help today!

had a very disappointing experience at this store. After bringing my puppy in for shots he had an allergic reaction that appeared to be related to the products or treatment used during his visit. What upset me the most it was how the staff handled it afterward.

When we returned to explain the situation, instead of showing concern or trying to help, the employees were rude, dismissive, and refused to take any accountability. As a pet owner, you trust a business to care for your animal safely, and when something goes wrong, you expect empathy and professionalism. Unfortunately, we received neither.

I would not recommend this place based on my experience. They don’t care for the way they handle concerns about the health and safety of the pets in their care.

I had one of the worst experiences at Vetco/Petco.

I originally went in for my dog's rabies vaccine. During the visit, the technician recommended another vaccine that she said my dog would likely need. Since they are the professionals, I trusted their recommendation and agreed.

I was told the total would be around $244, but that I had a coupon that would save me $86. When I went to pay, the cashier told me that wasn't true because part of the discount had already been applied during the visit, so only about $44 would actually be deducted. Instead of paying around $160 as I expected, I ended up paying about $200. The pricing was not explained clearly, and I felt misled.

The worst part happened after we left. About 30 minutes later, my dog had a severe reaction to the vaccines. He developed swelling, intense itching, red bumps all over his body, and started vomiting. I immediately called Petco, but they told me there was nothing they could do because the veterinarian had left just two minutes earlier. They told me to take him to the emergency vet and said someone would call me back.

The next day they called and instructed me to bring my dog back to the same Petco location. I had to miss work and waste more of my time. When I got there, they barely examined my dog and didn't provide any treatment. Then I was told that if my dog needed any medication or additional care because of the vaccine reaction, I would have to pay for it myself.

I don't think that's fair. My dog had a reaction after receiving vaccines they administered and recommended. I expected them to take responsibility, provide proper care, and show some compassion. Instead, I felt like no one cared. When I explained that I was missing work because they asked me to come back, the staff member simply told me, "If you're going to be late for work."

The lack of empathy, poor communication, and unwillingness to help after my dog experienced a vaccine reaction were extremely disappointing. I will not be returning, and I hope this review helps other pet owners know what to expect.

I’m a first time Kat Lady. Brought my kitten for her first visit, and the vet technician, Claire, was very nice and really took the time to educate me on how to take care of my little one.  I was very happy with my first visit.

Vet techs here are kind and nice I enjoyed their care. Pricing is fair, apts are plentiful.
However you can’t pick your Vet it’s just whoever is on. The first time I came I had a good experience. The second time I came I the veterinarian didn’t even introduce herself or even say hi, she just started rudely telling me all the things I was doing wrong taking care of my dog I could barely get a word in :(( of course there’s room for education for every pet parent but there’s ways to deliver information. Bedside manner was not good.

I brought my French bulldog to this Petco/Vetco because his paws were itchy and he needed help with allergies. The vet techs/nurses were great. They were kind, patient, and helped him calm down when he barked after they knocked on the door. My dog has anxiety at vet visits due to past experiences, but he is sweet, has never bitten anyone, and was doing fine with his toy.

The issue started when the actual vet came in. She was immediately rude, aggressive, and confrontational. She did not calmly approach my dog or give him space. She stood directly over him in an aggressive way, which made him bark even more. Instead of understanding that he was nervous, she acted annoyed and judgmental from the start.

She questioned me harshly about his heartworm medication, even after I explained I didn’t know the name but could call my regular vet to confirm it. She kept pushing the issue in a very rude tone, even though we were there for an allergy shot. The whole interaction felt more like she wanted to argue than actually help my dog.

Then she started making comments about us not having control of our dog, said his toy was just a distraction, and even compared how he should behave to a police dog. That was ridiculous. This is a small French bulldog with anxiety, not an aggressive dog. He did not bite, snap, or do anything dangerous. He barked because she came in with hostile energy and stood over him.

We ended up leaving without getting care because the vet was so unprofessional and disrespectful. As we walked out, she continued making comments about how my dog would need to be sedated before being seen. I have never had an experience like this at any vet clinic.

The techs/nurses were amazing, but the vet was horrible. Her attitude made it seem like she had no patience or compassion for anxious pets at all. It honestly felt like she did not even like dogs.

We took my Frenchie to Central Houston Animal Hospital right after, and the experience was completely different. They gave us way better service, everyone was kind and patient, and my dog was treated with care.

I would not recommend this place to anyone. Even if your dog does not bark, I still would not trust this vet based on how she treated us and how she handled the situation.

I had one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had with a veterinary clinic.

Yesterday, I brought my newly adopted kitten in for a free wellness exam as a new client. I had also noticed something unusual with his eye, so I wanted to make sure everything was okay. During the visit, the staff seemed kind, and the exam went smoothly. They gave him an antibiotic shot and eye treatment.

However, once we got home, I noticed black, coffee ground–like debris in his ears while playing with him. Later that evening, he also started scratching himself frequently. I took photos immediately and called the clinic the next day.

At first, the customer service representative was polite, but I had to wait a very long time before speaking to someone from the clinic. When I was finally connected, the technician who had seen my kitten was dismissive and spoke over me the entire time. She insisted they had already checked his ears and that nothing was there, and also said I never mentioned ear issues.

But that’s exactly the point of a wellness exam — I just adopted this kitten and I don’t know everything that might be wrong. I trusted them to do a thorough check. It was frustrating to hear them suggest the issue “must have appeared after,” especially when I had timestamped photos from the same day.

What disappointed me most was not just the oversight, but the attitude. There was no accountability, no apology, and no willingness to listen.

When I spoke with another staff member, I was told I would need to come back and pay for another wellness exam. That felt very unfair. If something was missed during the initial exam, I don’t think I should be charged again for the same issue. I was completely willing to pay for treatment or medication, but not for another exam due to their mistake.

This situation is especially upsetting because we trust veterinary clinics with the health of our pets. A little empathy, professionalism, and accountability would have made a huge difference.

Unfortunately, this experience left me very disappointed.

I came here a couple weeks ago with my cat and had a great experience. The vet, the front desk people, the techs; everything was amazing. So today when I brought in my 15 year old dog, Rowdy, with diarrhea today I assumed the same experience. The techs and front desk staff were still great. However, there a different vet today named Dr. McGovern and she was one of the most vile human being I have encountered in a long time. She was unempathetic, condescending, and straight up mean to me and my boyfriend. When I left the clinic, I was disappointed to the point of tears. The vet was making baseless claims about the severity of his “condition” only to find out she had yet to run any tests. Her only evidence was that “he was obviously in distress because he is panting and pacing”  which is completely normal for a dog at the vet who is stressed out and whose tummy hurts??  She was saying he “obviously” had anemia, again she had not run any tests. She had just looked at our dog. She then checked his heart and randomly said he had a heart murmur. Gave zero information on this, just stated it. Even though we had taken him to another vet just a few weeks ago and they said his heart was great. She made me and my boyfriend feel like we were the worst pet parents in the world and that we weren’t taking the condition seriously. (Which she never explained to us what that was. Just that it “could be a lot of things.”) When we were sitting there confused about what she was trying to tell us about Rowdy she actually said “okay so what is the money situation” as if we weren’t willing to give money to help our dog when were just genuinely confused. We told her we just wanted to run the fecal test and get some diarrheal medication and wait for the test results because he was acting completely normal otherwise. She then left the room in a hurry and never came back. She gave us no directive on the medicine. They have rotating vets at this clinic and Dr. Mary Sue McGovern is the worst of the worst, so I would just stay away from this practice altogether to not run the risk of experiencing her. She should lose her veterinarian license. I would highly recommend Sunset Animal Hospital off of Southwest Freeway instead. We went there and explained our situation to the front desk people and they were so nice and helped us understand what the medicine was and what to watch for.

UPDATE 8/17: Test came back positive for Hookworm. A very common easily treatable parasite. Symptoms include anemia, lethargy and diarrhea. This woman is completely off her rocker and should absolutely be stripped of her vet license.

The staff was very rude and did not even address any of the reasons we even made the appointment for. Instead they insisted the food we had been feeding our dog for years (and they knew she was eating, from our previous visits) was going to give her a heart condition and that pet food allergies were a myth and impossible to test for. It was $775 for the visit including the Symparica Trio, the test to see if our dog had symptoms of the heart condition that they insisted she had, a urine sample they had zero interest in collecting when our dog did her business outside, a probiotic because we mentioned she had thrown up a couple nights before, and a senior profile.

We wanted the senior check-up and blood test because we found a lump. After showing where the lump was, they insisted they could not feel the lump and disregarded the whole issue to focus more on the Fromm we were feeding our dog. It was a very confusing and upsetting time for us since we felt like we couldn't even communicate with the staff because they would run out every couple minutes and return with another employee. Update: providing this to help other pet owners. We went to a different vet when the lesions recurred. It turns out that the infection too was a misdiagnosis. It was an allergic reaction that rapidly improved with some anti-inflammatory treatment. The poor quality of care caused months of discomfort with the misdisgnosis, miscommunication and mishandling of this case. Considering how we were rushed without getting clear answers then, this is not surprising. I am glad we took our pet to the Cat Vet Clinic instead.

Original post: We had a bad experience with this clinic over the past 2 months. There are issues with communication, nursing staff, access to providers to have questions answered because of how busy they are:

1) Our cat was initially misdiagnosed with a simple skin abrasion, sent home with a wound ointment. The lesions recurred, we had to go back in 50 days and pay another examination fee.

2) When we arrived, there was no appointment on file. The call center failed to schedule us. No explanation was provided.

3) Our cat was diagnosed with a bacterial infection, but they did not hold the antibiotic. When asked to speak with the vet, the nurse said it would be a wait and tried to discourage me by saying the vet is seeing other patients. This was true, the vet was so busy going into other rooms that I would need to wait 20 mins to see her again. Meanwhile, I raised my issue with this system which limits my access to the provider: They will take your pet to a different area and examine all the pets there. Meanwhile, you are lucky to get a few mins with the actual vet to get your questions answered.

4) My feedback upset the nurse who raised her voice and said “Do you know we have been through a hurricane?”. All I wanted was to speak with the vet to see how long it would take for her to obtain the antibiotic. I was worried for my pet’s health but I was blamed by my nurse who brought up Hurricane Beryl.

5) When I went to the front desk and asked why I was not even scheduled for an appointment in the first place, the front desk told me: “it was not me, it was the call center’s fault”.

6) Finally I spoke with the vet, over an hour into the appointment. She told me about a reasonable difficulty with obtaining injection ingredients and said we can speak again tomorrow after she checks other locations. That is all I needed to hear. Except, it had turned into an emotional ordeal after going through all of the above.

I want my cat to receive antibiotic treatment tomorrow but after that, we will look for a different hospital.
We're thrilled to see that you gave us a high rating! Your support means a lot to us, and we're glad we could provide you with a positive experience.

The vet tech was also extremely rude, telling my girlfriend to not hold our cat while she was looking at him on the table and speaking over me as well.

The office manager, Hollie Lanphier, is also extremely unprofessional and said that she could not help resolve my issue because she was “not in the room.” When is she ever in the room? Why is she who customers are routed to for help when her response is that she wasn’t in the room? It
makes no sense that she would be in the room, seeing as though she is not a vet. I guess she just can’t help resolve any situation because she is never in the room.

Additionally, I was told by the front desk employee that the office manager (Hollie) was in a room taking care of a patient because they were short staffed on vet techs. I brought my cat into this facility because I am worried about her. I live on 600 a month disability and have no car. I was able to borrow the money for the test and had a coupon for the visit and got a ride. I even spoke with someone this morning on the phone because they were going to charge me 80 for visit and 180 for a worm test. After the call I was told the total should be 65. No one mentioned that if I didn’t bring her records she would have to get another rabies shot. It’s about how much money they can make. Thanks Petco. I really appreciate it.

If it weren't for the amazing techs/staff and convenience of having the store integration with veterinary services, I probably would not come back here. I brought my 4-year-old golden retriever in for routine vaccinations and a check-up, and the veterinarian, Dr. McGovern I believe was her name (this was our first time seeing her), was very condescending and rude. My dog is a very large full-bred golden retriever, and I am well aware that he has been gaining some weight. I have been actively making a lot of effort to get him outside and running/going on 2-3 mile walks a day in addition to placing him on specialized dietary food, however his energy levels have also decreased since being neutered. When she initially came into the room to see him, he attempted to run up to greet her (as he does with anyone) to which she cornered herself in the room and said, "Okay way too much enthusiasm" with a very smug face and did not come any closer to even touch him. She said very few words to me other than, "He is way too overweight", "How do you even walk this thing?" to which I explained the activity he gets and feeding schedule/description. She cut me off and just stated, "Well he probably can't run because he's so fat," then proceeded to hand me a feeding measurement cup and said other than that he looks great; the visit ended after that.

I understand that healthy weight is important in a dog to ensure longevity and prevention of any health issues but emphasizing that does not need to be done in such a condescending manner especially if you do not know the entire history. This was our first ever visit with this veterinarian, and if she knew his history and viewed his records, she would see that he has always been rather large for his size since he was born. I am not knocking her expertise and arguing in favor of overweight dogs at all, but I do think this should have been handled much more professionally - especially given that I explained all of the efforts that we have been making, and her only suggestion was to start cutting back more on his food right before she walked out the room.

Outside of this, the staff at this location go above and beyond in making sure that you and your pet are comfortable and I am very appreciative of them and their kindness. I felt important to share this here because of how much effort the team there puts into making sure everyone feels welcomed and has a positive experience and just wanted to highlight how disappointing it is that one can still have a pretty bad experience despite their efforts due to the treatment by the veterinarian themselves.
Very friendly, very helpful and they definitely follow up with any services, procedures or test results that you have pending. Very friendly!

We took my beagle-terrier mix for a sick visit. He had been having runny stools with blood for 2 days. I just wanted a veterinarian who expressed the same concern about my sick puppy as I have. After a negative parvo test and fecal sample we are awaiting results from, Dr. Cleary offered no solutions and was very condescending from the moment she walked in for the exam. She asked if we know if he had been in the garbage or eating inedible objects? Other than stuffing from worn toys, nothing came to mind. He doesn’t regularly go through the trash can for his dinner. What was most upsetting is they kept trying to get his temperature through rectum, 3 times at most. While I understand this may have been the most logical route due to his symptoms, why not check it through his ear to at least rule out a fever? May I remind you he has been bleeding from his rectum! Dr. cleary called him a “dramatic little beagle” as they tussled to get his temperature. No treats were offered to calm him. She offered no helpful reccomendations and had an overall sense of disinterest in helping my pup recover. Everything else just seemed like a cash grab.. Aside from the vet techs and receptionist a 1/10 experience and I would not reccomend Dr. Cleary for any pet owners seeking answers. We will be visiting another vet if his symptoms persist after we implement a low fat diet.
